model.rationale: TX-25 leans Republican by eleven points, Williams is an incumbent with over $1 million on hand, and Sims shows no measurable fundraising or polling presence. Markets price a Republican win near 96%, consistent with a Safe R call.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Sims within single digits or a major outside-spending surge would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Roger Williams seeks another term in a central Texas district that voted Republican by eleven points at the presidential level. He enters the general election with a well-funded campaign, over a million dollars in cash, while Democrat Dione Sims has reported no fundraising activity. No public polls or expert race ratings are available for the contest.

Prediction markets give Williams roughly a 96% chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals leave little room for an upset absent an extraordinary shift. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the winner.
